concern_results.conclusion: Step 4's suppression-location rule matches the cited tsc 6.0.3 behavior and does not contradict item 3 or the strictness-migration rule; the register row is append-only with the ledger's field grammar; summary numbers recompute against run1/run2 analysis.md and deprecation-check.jsonl (4/10 then 5/10 unfixed, 0/10 before and fixed; coverage +0.09..+0.19; Fisher one-sided p≈0.016 checks out).

No secrets, host paths, or personal data in committed evidence (paths generalized, test emails moved to example domains, deviations disclosed); arms ran tool-restricted under bwrap with parent-session env stripped; judges fence answers as untrusted data and fail closed.

Both judges retry once then record error rows rather than guessing; failed arm runs write meta only and are excluded; the driver resumes by signature and stops at the utilization threshold; known residuals (maintained tool's --allowedTools weakness, one harmless cache glob) are disclosed instead of hidden.

Oracle answers separate known-good/known-bad for both judges; 10 valid observations per arm per fixture with permutation tests; headline claims trace to committed aggregates, but the wrong-facts attribution and per-run parameters rest on files absent from the candidate (finding below).

Only step 4 changes in the skill reference; SKILL.md, sibling skills, tasks and rubrics untouched; the earlier validation.md text is preserved with only a dated append; new evidence directories carry their own AGENTS.md as the root contract requires.
Claims are bounded to one model, a named same-family judge, spot-checked human:true fixtures, and per-fixture aggregates; no absolutes or universals beyond the committed evidence.

New contract files state scope, boundaries and validation without loosening parent rules, and no quoted rule names a dead command; however behavior-eval/AGENTS.md describes frozen contents that are not in the candidate, and summary.md cites a layers filename the harness never writes (findings below).
